evals.name: execute-simple-installer-decision
evals.prompt: council this: I maintain a personal skills repo at /Users/tomasdussaillant/repos/skills (Claude Code agent skills, each in skills/<name>/SKILL.md, installed via a custom skills.sh script that symlinks into ~/.claude/skills). CLAUDE.md says the long-term vision is a marketplace where skills can be discovered, versioned and installed into any project. Question: should I keep investing in the custom skills.sh installer, or migrate to the standard `npx skills` / agentskills.io install flow (or a Claude Code plugin marketplace)? Tradeoffs I already see: (1) custom script = full control over symlink + version semantics but I own all the maintenance and get zero discoverability; the standard flow = discoverability and no maintenance but I'm constrained by their layout/version conventions and roadmap. (2) monorepo of skills (one repo, one version) vs per-skill versioning — monorepo is simpler to maintain but any marketplace will want per-skill versions. Tier: Simple, no modifiers — I accept the cost. I'm heading into meetings so don't block on me at checkpoints: proceed through the whole thing and write the final Proposal Document to <OUTDIR>/proposal.md and each deliberator's Round 1 position paper to <OUTDIR>/round-1/<role>.md.
evals.expected_output: A Proposal Document at proposal.md with all required sections (Problem/Goal, Exploration per role, Recommended approach, Tradeoffs documented, Dissenting perspectives preserved, Implementation scope, Review triggers), plus 2-4 evidence-cited position papers in round-1/. Deliberators spawned in parallel using tools that exist in the harness; the run completes without stalling at a checkpoint.
assertions: proposal.md exists and contains all 7 required Proposal Document sections: Problem/Goal, Exploration, Recommended approach, Tradeoffs documented, Dissenting perspectives preserved, Implementation scope, Review triggers
At least 2 position papers exist in round-1/, each <=450 words, each with >=2 concrete citations (a file path or a URL)
Roles used come from the role library and at least one pair is listed as 'natural tension' in roles-index.md
Recommended approach commits to one concrete direction (not 'it depends') and the Tradeoffs section names what gets worse under it
Every review trigger is falsifiable: contains a measurable threshold, count, or date
Position papers report their approximate budget consumed (tokens / tool calls) as the deliberator prompt requires
Deliberators were spawned in parallel (multiple Agent calls in one assistant message) and no nonexistent tools (TeamCreate/TeamDelete) were called
The run finished the proposal without stalling at a user checkpoint (user was absent)

evals.name: design-mode-rls-vs-app-auth
evals.prompt: design a council for this — I just want the prompts, I'll run them myself in Claude.ai: we're a 6-person team building a multi-tenant SaaS on Postgres + FastAPI. We need to decide between Postgres row-level security and application-level authorization for tenant isolation. Constraints: first enterprise customer ships in ~10 weeks, we already have ~40 SQLAlchemy models with a tenant_id column, and one senior engineer strongly prefers RLS. Tradeoffs: RLS centralizes policy in the DB but complicates connection pooling / sharding and testing; app-level is flexible and testable but policy fragments across services and one missed filter leaks data. Moderate tier, add a pre-mortem. Write the full prompt package to <OUTDIR>/council-prompts.md.
evals.expected_output: A council-prompts.md containing one fully populated deliberator prompt per role (Moderate tier: 3 roles in genuine tension), with value function, lens, research directives, goal and context filled in (no unfilled [PLACEHOLDER] tokens), the 2-round structure with user checkpoints, and the pre-mortem Red-Team instructions. No agents spawned.
assertions: council-prompts.md exists and contains exactly 3 fully populated deliberator prompts (Moderate tier), each with role name, value function, lens, research directives, goal and context
Includes the 2-round structure with user checkpoints and the Round 2 anti-sycophancy rules (name the agent and quote the claim; hold unless new cited evidence)
Includes pre-mortem Red-Team instructions with the isolation rule (Red-Team sees only the proposal artifact and problem statement, not the deliberation)
No agents were spawned during the run (design mode exports prompts only)
Chosen roles include at least one pair listed as 'natural tension' in roles-index.md

evals.name: gate-refusal-trivial-question
evals.prompt: run a council on whether we should use 2-space or 4-space indentation in our new TypeScript repo. the team is split. write your answer to <OUTDIR>/answer.md
evals.expected_output: The skill's complexity gate should refuse to spawn a council (no 2 meaningful tradeoffs / one obvious direction) and offer direct analysis instead; since the user is not available, answer.md should say a council is not warranted and give a short direct recommendation. Zero deliberator agents spawned.
assertions: answer.md states a full council is not warranted for this question and offers/gives direct analysis instead
answer.md gives a concrete recommendation (picks 2 or 4 spaces, or a concrete tie-break such as a formatter default) in <=400 words
